followup_rationale: No follow-up is proposed. Nearby nilpotent-target conjectures are pre-existing questions, and simply changing the field, target class or unimodularity condition supplies neither a new conjecture nor a sufficiently developed research mechanism. The review does not meet the high bar for adding a separate public research direction.
key_boundaries: The published theorem is stated for finite-dimensional complex Lie algebras. It does not provide a separate treatment of arbitrary real forms, positive characteristic or infinite dimension.
Unimodularity cannot simply be omitted. Remark 4 supplies a three-dimensional nonunimodular solvable source with two homomorphisms into sl₂(C) whose difference is invertible.

A merely reductive target is not covered. Central directions change both the inner-derivation reduction and the topological obstruction; earlier literature contains perfect-source examples with reductive nonsemisimple targets.

The orbit map identifies manifolds, and is not asserted to be a group homomorphism. The proof’s conclusion is semisimplicity of the source; a Lie algebra isomorphism is not inferred solely from that manifold identification.

The determinant method, transverse-pair formulation and Lie-theoretic and topological inputs have substantial predecessors. The literature comparison is bounded, and the original body of Onishchik’s 1969 decomposition paper was not accessible in this review. No exhaustive novelty or first-priority certificate is given.

Exact finite diagnostic checks accompany the paper. They cannot establish the global integration, transitivity, covering-space or homology arguments, which depend on the analytical proof and its cited classical results.
